subject: Follow-up: LLM routing & policy onboarding questions
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex@rainbridge.ai>, Priya Suresh <priya@rainbridge.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap + concrete asks from today's call (routing, SDK, auth)

Alex / Priya — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap of the main threads we discussed and a few clarifying questions so your engineers can choose the right onboarding path. High-level ask: can we confirm the three items below by EOD Thursday so we can finalize the PoC plan?

1) SDK & auth model
- You indicated preference for SDK integration (Python + Node). We can offer our hosted SDK with API key auth for the PoC, or we can provision a short-lived mTLS credential for a private deployment. Which would your security team prefer to start with?

2) Routing & latency policy goals
- Target p95 generation latency: <= 250ms for short prompts (<= 256 tokens).
- Cost window: target <= $0.003/token equivalent for production after optimization.
- We proposed a two-tier fallback chain (high-quality model -> quantized low-cost model -> cached prefix response). Confirm if the priority is latency over cost or vice versa.

3) Structured output / tool calling
- You asked about tool calling for EHR lookups: Redwood supports function-like structured output and a secure tool invocation pattern. Will the PoC include simulated tool calls or a dummy EHR endpoint we can exercise?

Optional notes / asks for engineering:
- Embeddings & reranker: are you planning similarity search over notes (approx size and daily QPS would help)? We recommend 1536-d embeddings for short clinical notes; we can show cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Region preference: you mentioned US-West for data residency. Confirm if all traffic should stay in us-west-2.

Attachments: I attached a rough onboarding MVP workbook, and an example routing policy JSON that maps to the fallback chain we discussed.

Next steps (suggested):
- You confirm SDK/auth path, region, and priority (latency v cost).
- We send a short technical runbook and a draft mutual action plan.
- Schedule a follow-up with your platform engineer (30–45m) to walk the SDK quickstart and run a sample.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com | (415) 555-0132

---
Attachments: rb-mapp-onboarding-mvp.xlsx (workbook), example-routing-policies.json (policy examples)
From: Alex Chen <alex@rainbridge.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Suresh <priya@rainbridge.ai>, engineering@rainbridge.ai
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 17:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + concrete asks from today's call (routing, SDK, auth)

Thanks, Soojin — good summary. Quick answers inline below.

1) SDK & auth model
- For PoC let's do API key via hosted SDK (Node) to move fast; security will ask for mTLS later.

2) Routing & latency policy goals
- Priority is latency (user-facing triage). 250ms p95 is aggressive but aligns with our product goals. We can accept higher cost for the initial PoC.

3) Structured output / tool calling
- We'll provide a staging EHR stub endpoint (read-only) that your SREs can hit. It will be available under engineering@rainbridge.ai creds; I'll share the stub URL once we confirm auth approach.

Embeddings & reranker
- We expect ~25k notes in the initial index and ~400 QPS at peak for similarity queries. We'll likely run an L2 reranker stage for top-10 candidates.

Region
- us-west-2 only for now.

We'll confirm formally by Thursday. Can you include the example of a fallback chain mapping to our p95 target? That will help Priya's team.

—Alex
Alex Chen
Head of Platform, Rainbridge Health
alex@rainbridge.ai

Alex / Priya — attached is a short runbook and a concrete fallback policy example that maps an incoming request to:
- path A: low-latency specialization model (p95 <= 220ms)
- path B: quantized 8-bit model (p95 <= 450ms, cost down 3x)
- path C: prefix cache response (instant for repeated prompts)

Key notes in the runbook:
- SDK quickstart (Node) with example auth header and minimal retry/backoff policy.
- How to enable structured output and safe function calling for EHR lookups (we include sample JSON schema).
- Embedding pipeline: recommended vector dimension, batching, and nightly index rebuild pattern.

Action items for Rainbridge (if you confirm API key PoC):
- Share a staging API key or request a temporary one from me.
- Confirm the EHR stub URL and any IP allowlist.
- Provide a spreadsheet column with average note length and expected daily ingests (I put an example tab in the workbook).

I'll let Marcus and Karthik add any infra-specific guidance below.

Best,
Soojin

Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + concrete asks from today's call (routing, SDK, auth) — infra notes

Hi Priya / Alex — quick infra notes from our side to keep the PoC low friction: 

- SDK auth: temporary API keys are simplest for the PoC. We will emit key usage logs for your audit, and can rotate keys daily if needed.
- Region routing: we'll pin the PoC to us-west-2 and enforce egress controls back to your VPC if you choose Private deployment later.
- Latency policy enforcement: Redwood can enforce a hard timeout at the routing layer; if a model doesn't meet the p95 threshold, traffic is automatically shifted to the next candidate for that route. We'll show simulated load tests.
- Reranker/embeddings: for 25k notes, expect embedding creation to take ~20–30 minutes for a full rebuild with sensible batching; incremental updates are near-real time. We recommend storing vectors in your Redis/FAISS cluster — we can provide connector examples.

I'll schedule a short infra run-through demo once you confirm the PoC auth path.

Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

From: Priya Suresh <priya@rainbridge.ai>

Thanks — this looks good. Confirming the PoC decisions from Rainbridge:
- API key + hosted SDK (Node) for PoC
- us-west-2 region only
- Priority: latency first; we accept higher cost for initial evaluation
- We will provide: EHR stub URL (read-only), sample note CSV (avg length column included), and a contact for a network allowlist (IP ranges will be posted by EOD Friday).

Next step: can you send the temporary API key and a calendar invite for a 45-minute SDK onboarding session (propose Mon 2027-05-10 10:00am PT)?

Priya Suresh
